newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pacific BBA sees 97 profit well ahead of 96.
newsitem.headline: Pacific BBA sees 97 profit well ahead of 96.

text.p: Automotive parts maker Pacific BBA Ltd said on Wednesday that it expected earnings for calendar 1997 to be well ahead of the 1996 year.

"The company's outlook is very positive, despite the Australian economy remaining flat. We expect 1997 to be a good year with earnings well ahead of 1996," chairman Bruce Lithgow told shareholders at the annual meeting.

"The planning and investment over recent times will yield greater earnings from 1997 and for the rest of the decade," Lithgow said. Pacific BBA reported a 6.1 percent rise in net profit in 1996 to A$16.87 million.

"While we anticipate only slow improvement in the Australian economy, we see continued expansion in most overseas markets," Lithgow said. He said the automotive unit's global business would continue to build up strongly in the rest of 1997.

He said that although the plastics unit was performing to budget, year to date, some units were still not performing satisfactorily and would continue to receive close management attention. "The construction and industrial products division is planning for strong and sustained growth and we see it becoming a much greater force in our overall plans for the future."
Lithgow said the company plans a name change.
"We believe the company's identity will be enhanced by shedding reference to our past ownership," Lithgow said.
The UK company, BBA Group Plc, divested its majority interest in 1993 and it was time to adopt a name which was more relevant to the Company today, he said.
At 11.55 a.m. (0155 GMT), Pacific BBA shares were six cents firmer at A$4.76.
